blocks.content: Open Traces Drilldown to investigate a request from its overall patterns down to individual spans.
Open Traces Drilldown to start investigating requests without writing a query.
blocks.tooltip: Start with a populated Tempo investigation.

blocks.content: You are ready to choose the requests you want to investigate.
Scope your requests to a Tempo datasource, time range, and service, then compare traffic, failures, and latency.

blocks.title: Scope requests and compare RED metrics

blocks.content: Choose an existing Tempo datasource with trace data; use the datasource name from your own stack.
blocks.tooltip: Choose a source that contains the requests you want to investigate.

blocks.content: Choose a time range containing traces and refresh the data, then wait for populated results before continuing. An error or empty result is not a successful investigation.
blocks.tooltip: Use a time window with trace data and wait for results to load.

blocks.content: Select **Root spans** to focus on the top-level request of each trace rather than every operation within it.
blocks.tooltip: Focus on the top-level request of each trace.

blocks.content: Add a **service.name** filter and choose a real service value from your datasource, then wait for matching data. This keeps the comparisons focused on one service.
blocks.tooltip: Narrow the results to a service with trace data.

blocks.content: Select **Rate** and inspect the matching root spans per second to understand how much request traffic falls within your scope.
blocks.tooltip: Inspect how much matching request traffic arrives each second.

blocks.content: Select **Errors** to compare failures within the same service and time range.
blocks.tooltip: Look for failures without changing the scope of your investigation.

blocks.content: Select **Duration** to investigate request latency within the same scope.
blocks.tooltip: Look at how long the matching requests take.

blocks.content: You have compared request rate, errors, and duration for the same service and time window.
Follow the latency patterns through attribute comparisons and service structure to a real trace.

blocks.title: Inspect latency and open a trace

blocks.content: Select **Breakdown** to compare latency across attributes while keeping your current scope.
blocks.tooltip: Compare latency across attributes to find differences worth investigating.

blocks.content: Inspect the attribute breakdown and look for differences in latency; this is an observation, so no selection is needed.
blocks.tooltip: Look for attribute values whose latency differs from the others.

blocks.content: Select **Root cause latency** to inspect the service structure behind the matching traces.
blocks.tooltip: Move from attribute comparisons to the structure of the requests.

blocks.content: Inspect the service structure and where latency accumulates; no state change is needed here.
blocks.tooltip: Look for where time accumulates across the request structure.

blocks.content: Select **Slow traces** to move from the overall patterns to individual matching requests.
blocks.tooltip: Find an individual request to inspect in detail.

blocks.content: Choose a visible trace name in the populated list, not its external-link icon, to open the trace drawer. If no traces match, adjust your data scope and repeat the investigation.
blocks.tooltip: Open a request by its name so you can inspect its spans here.

blocks.content: Inspect the opened trace and its spans in the drawer; no further selection is needed to confirm you reached a real request.
blocks.tooltip: Confirm that the selected request has loaded and its spans are visible.

blocks.content: You have completed the investigation when your Tempo results cover the chosen time range and root spans, you have compared the RED metrics and inspected breakdown and service structure, and a selected trace displays its spans in the drawer.
